newsitem.title: UK: Late trade spares IPE natgas from another blank day.
newsitem.headline: Late trade spares IPE natgas from another blank day.

text.p: The IPE's natural gas contract was spared from suffering a third straight day without any trade at all, when three deals were done just before the close of the afternoon session on Wednesday.
The first trades of the week were done four minutes before the close of trading on Wednesday, when the fourth quarter was traded in what appeared to be a strip deal.
October was done at 13.90 pence a therm, up 0.310 pence from Tuesday's settlement, with November done at 14.60 pence and December at 15.30 pence. A total of 30 lots were traded, 10 in each month.
At one point on Wednesday afternoon there were no bids or offers posted at all for any of the contract's 12 months.

But later in the afternoon there was some active movement of bids and offers. By the close ranges were tighter in some periods than they have been recently, with front month June bid at 11.50 pence a therm against an offer at 11.75 pence.
